ops.title: GraphiteRepo swallows gitCommonDir errors — refuted as a defect, worth knowing
ops.body:
A review finding claimed `gitCommonDir` (`internal/vcs/vcs.go:87-97`) is defective for using raw `exec.CommandContext(...).Output()` instead of the `render.RunCLI*` family, which alone wraps stderr into the returned error. An adversarial refutation pass **refuted it as a defect with impact**, and the reasoning is worth keeping.

The code fact is true, and there is no import-cycle reason — `internal/vcs` already imports `internal/render` in `github.go` (`render.RunCLIDir` at `:159`, `:226`). But the only call site is `GraphiteRepo` (`vcs.go:69-83`), which does `common, err := gitCommonDir(ctx, root); if err != nil { return false }` — the error is discarded outright, never logged, never surfaced. `gitCommonDir` has no other callers. So whether stderr is captured changes nothing anyone can observe: a real style inconsistency with zero behavioural consequence.

**The residual concern is a different one, and not what the finding named.** `GraphiteRepo` collapsing every error into `false` means a permissions problem or a corrupted `.git` file reads as "this repo has no Graphite config" — a silent false negative in exactly the detection the linked-worktree fix was added to repair. That shape predates this change set and was left alone deliberately rather than widened mid-review. Anyone revisiting `GraphiteRepo` should decide whether a lookup failure deserves to be distinguishable from a genuine absence.
